title: Sunny and the Blue Tongue Lizard
description: Little Sonny the quokka has a slow, patient meeting with a wise old blue tongue lizard. A calm, curious bedtime story for little ones. Part of Sonny's Cozy Quokka Bedtime Tales.
narration:
One quiet afternoon, Sunny was making his way along the sunny path when he noticed something very still on a flat warm rock.

A blue tongue lizard.

It was big, as lizards go — long and slow and scaly, with a body the colour of dry bark and small, steady eyes. Its belly was low to the warm rock. It didn't move at all.

Sunny stopped.

He had seen blue tongue lizards before, but always from a distance. He sat down very slowly, a little way away, and looked.

The lizard looked back.

Its eyes were copper-coloured and very calm. It didn't seem bothered by Sunny at all. It just blinked, once, slowly, and kept its position on the warm stone.

Sunny waited.

After a long moment, the lizard opened its mouth just slightly, and stuck out its tongue. It was a deep, vivid blue — the most surprising colour in all this quiet brown and green bush.

Sunny's eyes went wide.

The tongue disappeared again. The lizard closed its mouth.

Sunny and the lizard looked at each other.

Somehow Sunny felt as though the lizard was very old and very wise, and had seen many things, and was in no hurry whatsoever.

Sunny decided to feel the same way.

They sat together in the warm afternoon sun for a long, peaceful time.

Finally, without any hurry, the lizard turned and made its slow way off the rock and into the low, dry grass.

Sunny watched it go.

He pressed his paw to his cheek and thought that he had never had such a quiet and interesting conversation in all his life.

Goodnight, little Sunny. Goodnight, blue tongue lizard. Goodnight, warm and patient afternoon.
